study type: Retrospective cohort study using a differences-in-differences analysis
exposure: Affordable Care Act (ACA) dependent coverage provision
outcome: Infant neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission rate
cohort: Live births among US women aged 24-25 years (exposure group) and 27-28 years (control group) before (2009) and after (2011-2013) enactment of the ACA dependent coverage provision
finding: The ACA's dependent coverage provision was associated with an increase in private insurance coverage for births, improved prenatal care utilization, and a modest reduction in preterm births, but no significant changes in cesarean delivery rates, low birth weight, or NICU admissions.
